title: Can you give three ratios that match four to nine?
description: Both terms of four to nine are multiplied by the same number, three times over, to make three proportional ratios. Each is checked by dividing back by the factor.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying both terms by one number keeps the ratio proportional. Watch for students who add the same number to both terms.

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 2)
video_script.why: The child makes proportional ratios by multiplying both terms by one factor.
video_script.substitution: Pick a factor, multiply both terms of 4 : 9 by it, and check by dividing back.
video_script.anchor: the ratio 4 : 9 on the board with three empty ratio boxes beside it
video_script.payoff_line: Eight to eighteen, twelve to twenty seven, and sixteen to thirty six all match four to nine.

final_answer.spoken: for example eight to eighteen, twelve to twenty seven, and sixteen to thirty six

maths_rules: any other whole number as the factor also works, so the answer is one example
video_script.design: One idea: one factor on both terms gives a proportional ratio. Uses the factor of change from the solved example. The ratio 4 : 9 stays for the whole video.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about ratios.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is four to nine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you give three more ratios that match it?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 4 : 9 with an arrow × factor landing on both terms; the words proportional beside the new ratio

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='prop'/>Ratios with the same simplest form are called proportional.
<bookmark mark='fac'/>Multiply both terms by one number, and the new ratio stays proportional.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ratio four to nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: three ratios proportional to 4 : 9

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three ratios proportional to four to nine.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Step one, multiply both terms by two.
<bookmark mark='m'/>Four times two is eight, and nine times two is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is eight to eighteen.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Step two, multiply both terms by three.
<bookmark mark='m'/>Four times three is twelve, and nine times three is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is twelve to twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Step three, multiply both terms by four.
<bookmark mark='m'/>Four times four is sixteen, and nine times four is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is sixteen to thirty six.

marks.chk: the words Check: divide back are written

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check by dividing each ratio back by its factor.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Eight and eighteen divided by two give four and nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Twelve and twenty seven divided by three give four and nine.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Sixteen and thirty six divided by four give four and nine.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Eight to eighteen, twelve to twenty seven, and sixteen to thirty six all match four to nine.
